title: Managed ETH product terms and controls: presentation review
status: Publisher disclosures reviewed; deployed controls and legal rights remain explicitly scoped
method: Opened official publisher pages directly. Fresh disclosures are a separate presentation layer and do not change frozen T quantities. Quotations limited to at most 25 words per publisher site. No transaction, wallet connection, simulation or account access.

sources.title: Typical Liquid withdrawal timelines
sources.quote: estimated processing time, not a guaranteed deadline
facts: The current support estimate for Liquid ETH is up to 3 days.
Timing depends on available liquidity, queue demand, strategy operations and settlement.
A completed historical withdrawal does not guarantee the timing of the next request.
sources.scope: Observed support policy, not the withdrawal queue's deployed state at snapshot T.
unresolved: No successful withdrawal was executed or simulated in this review.
No independent percentile distribution of completed withdrawal times was reconstructed.

sources.title: How to Withdraw From Liquid
facts: The user selects Earn, selects the vault, enters an amount and submits a withdrawal transaction.
The guide says processed proceeds arrive automatically without a manual claim.
The Liquid ETH example asks the user to choose a requested output asset such as wETH or weETH.
sources.scope: Front-end workflow. This does not prove the same assets are enabled in every underlying queue contract.
unresolved: The older guide uses deadline language that is stronger than the newer explicit estimate.
The exact wETH route differs from the weETH-only checked queue at T and needs a route-level simulation.

sources.title: How Liquid works
facts: Liquid automates allocation, rebalancing and compounding.
A strategy can touch several protocols, so protocol exposure percentages may exceed 100%.
The support guide says Liquid is unavailable in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom.
Vault-specific platform fees are disclosed in the vault fact sheet; a generic product fee range is not an ETH vault rate.
sources.scope: General Liquid UI policy. Do not replace the 35 bp rate verified at T with the generic fee range.
unresolved: The product-specific contemporary fact sheet was not separately captured in this review.
Jurisdiction policy and enforceable user-specific eligibility are distinct.

sources.title: Terms of Use
facts: Section 4 says Liquid assets are placed into Veda vaults and allocated to other DeFi protocols.
The terms incorporate Veda's separate terms for Liquid vault services.
The provider reserves the ability to alter its price plan and fees.
The terms disclaim fiduciary obligations and allow interface/service access to be suspended or ended.
Points are described as a limited licence, with no contractual currency equivalent or redemption entitlement.
sources.scope: Summary of publisher terms, not a legal opinion or a finding that every disclaimer is enforceable.
unresolved: Veda's incorporated terms were not separately reviewed.
The legal terms do not identify the actual holders of Liquid ETH on-chain permissions.
No promise of redemption by a fixed date was established.

sources.title: Veda Core Components
sources.quote: Users can cancel unfulfilled requests at any time to reclaim their shares.
facts: The BoringVault holds assets and executes calls; modules enforce the surrounding rules.
The Teller uses the Accountant rate for minting and redemption, with deployment-specific share locks.
The Accountant receives off-chain rate updates with frequency and deviation bounds; bounds can pause updates.
The Manager verifies permitted targets, functions and parameters against per-strategist Merkle trees.
The BoringQueue transfers requested shares to the queue, waits for maturity and lets solvers exchange underlying assets for those shares.
Queue maturity, solver deadline and discount range are configurable by asset.
sources.scope: Framework description. Cancellation and module controls need confirmation against the exact deployed Liquid ETH variants before being promised to users.
unresolved: This fresh document review alone does not map every authorised actor, Merkle-root updater, pause key, fee setter or bypass path. Use the separate fixed-block capability reconstruction for those facts.
The 24-hour authority-owner timelock verified at T must not be treated as a universal delay on every fee, rate or pause action.

sources.title: Getting Started With Fluid Lite
facts: Users select the deposited vault, choose Withdraw, enter the ETH/stETH amount and confirm in their wallet.
The user guide presents the return as a transfer to the wallet after confirmation.
The guide discloses a 0.05% exit fee directed to the DAO.
sources.scope: Published user workflow. Instant language must be qualified by pause and liquidity conditions documented separately.
unresolved: No large exit was simulated, including the unwind routes needed to deliver native ETH.
The guide does not establish a management/performance fee of zero.
Current displayed fee policy is not the full historical fee ledger.

sources.title: Risks
sources.quote: Rebalancers do not have the ability to withdraw funds from the vault.
facts: DAO governance sets parameters and leverage ranges and can approve or remove protocols.
Governance appoints permissioned rebalancers, who can leverage and refinance within configured limits.
The team multisig can reduce a protocol ratio, pause withdrawals temporarily and pause rebalancing.
The page identifies the team multisig as 0xa8c31E39e40E6765BEdBd83D92D6AA0B33f1CCC5 and says it cannot withdraw or move vault funds.
Automation may refinance or sell collateral to repay debt; deleveraging can crystallise slippage losses.
The page asks users to accept parameter, setting and code changes.
sources.scope: Publisher description of governance and emergency roles, not a complete deployed access-control proof.
unresolved: Safe threshold, owners, timelock and function-selector permissions were not independently mapped here.
Permission to alter modules or fees was not established from this page.
Underlying-protocol governance adds separate controls.

sources.title: Redemption Process
facts: The fetched current page defines the Curve redemption band as 0 to 50 wstETH.
Within the band, the dApp can route redemption through a tETH/wstETH Curve swap.
Above the band, normal redemption burns tETH and leads to a wstETH claim after approximately 7 days.
The estimated front-end payout is adjusted by the lower tETH/wstETH rate and a minimum/maximum underlying conversion ratio across initiation and finalisation.
Normal redemption charges 5 bp to cover interest during the wait.
Unwinding can include LST redemption to native ETH and loan repayment before wstETH becomes claimable.
The redemption band is a governance-controlled parameter.
Fastlane is capacity limited and the fetched current page discloses a 0.5% fee in the redeemed asset.
sources.scope: Current policy and formula disclosure. Search-index versions showing a 200 wstETH band or 2% Fastlane are stale relative to the opened page.
unresolved: No fixed-block getter for the band, fee and delay was independently checked here.
The page's numerical worked example mixes a 200 tETH narrative with 50 in the formula and inconsistent subtraction; use the symbolic formula only.
A Curve sale also requires a market quote and slippage, separate from queued redemption fees.

sources.title: Fees
sources.quote: Only applied when MEY is positive.
facts: The performance policy is 20% of positive Market Effective Yield.
The fee is collected in the base pool token before a profit/loss rebase.
The fetched current Fastlane policy is 0.5% in the underlying LST.
The documentation says Pendle YT-tETH and LP-tETH redemptions are automatically routed through Fastlane.
sources.scope: Policy disclosure. MEY is not automatically equivalent to all staking income; integration-specific actual routes still need verification.
unresolved: Historical fee changes and deployed route-specific rates remain open.

sources.title: Timelock
facts: The documentation describes a five-day timelock for critical governance actions, including vault logic upgrades and fee changes.
It says upcoming changes are visible on-chain before execution.
sources.scope: General governance description. It is not independent confirmation of the implementation, actor set or every emergency exception.
unresolved: The exact timelock contract, proposer/executor/canceller members, proxy admin and pause rights remain unmapped.
A five-day notice window is shorter than the approximately seven-day normal exit estimate; notice does not establish a completed exit before change. This comparison is an analytical inference.

sources.title: Safety Mechanisms
facts: Protocol-owned peg support can use insurance-fund ETH to purchase and burn tETH.
The page describes assistance for some daily rebalancing shortfalls.
Risk-event compensation is described as potential, with coverage decisions initially made by the protocol and future governance.
sources.scope: Disclosed support mechanisms; they are not a blanket insurance promise.
unresolved: Fund size, actual deployed coverage limits and enforceable claimant rights were not independently verified.

rsETH-to-ETH recovery is a separate underlying step.

sources.title: Concrete Upgradable Multisig and Queue Changes security assessment
facts: The reviewed code includes configurable whitelist controls, strategy allocation, fees and multisignature custody.
The maxRedeem finding says a queue-mode maximum share redemption is not a promise of immediate liquidity and delivered assets are reduced by withdrawal fees.
The disclosed code can return zero redeemable shares when paused, withdrawals are paused or the user is not whitelisted.
sources.scope: Only the reviewed commit and contracts in the audit. The dossier's two products execute ConcreteInitMintableAsyncVaultImpl / ConcreteAsyncVaultImpl; equivalence to the audited ConcreteMultiStrategyVault was not established.
unresolved: Do not label the described audit findings as active bugs in either ETH product without code matching.
The audit cannot substitute for product-specific executed withdrawal rights.

sources.title: Ribbon Theta vaults architecture
facts: The documented ETH call vault locks ETH as option collateral, auctions call options and receives ETH premiums from buyers.
An in-the-money settlement returns less ETH collateral, while an out-of-the-money settlement releases the collateral.
Standard exits use initiateWithdraw and completeWithdraw after weekly rollover; instant exits only cover unused pending deposits.
The owner can set fees, fee recipient and deposit cap and controls lifecycle actions; the admin can upgrade the implementation; both roles are documented as multisigs.
sources.scope: A documented historical example of ETH volatility selling, not a verified active product or quantified market segment at T.
unresolved: Current activity, current configuration and complete T capital/history were not verified.
Do not count option notional as ETH principal.

sources.title: DOV Trading and options
sources.quote: in the money weeks are excluded
facts: The documented fee schedule is 2% annual management and 10% performance in profitable weeks; the FAQ says fees are included in displayed performance.
The projected APY uses an average of four annualised weekly observations but excludes in-the-money weeks.
Call settlements use the collateral asset and the FAQ says the strategy is not delta neutral.
A vault share is not a fixed 1:1 claim on ETH.
sources.scope: Historical documentation, not a fresh active product quote. The APY definition is useful evidence of why premium yield must not be equated with total return.
unresolved: Current deployment fees and operational availability remain unverified.

sources.title: How to withdraw
facts: A queued withdrawal remains exposed to that week's gains or losses.
The guide says queued requests cannot be cancelled.
LST vault withdrawals deliver their LST collateral rather than native ETH.
Completion time depends on settlement dispute periods and option auctions; deprecated vaults may require operator action.
sources.scope: Historical Ribbon workflow; not a promise about present operational availability.
unresolved: No withdrawal or live vault interaction was performed.

inferences.claim: The advertised five-day governance notice is shorter than the estimated seven-day normal redemption path, so notice alone does not guarantee an exit completes before a change.
The guide's instant withdrawal language should be read together with documented pause rights and deleveraging losses, rather than as an unconditional liquidity guarantee.
Option premiums pay the holder for transferring upside and volatility risk. A premiums-based projected APY that excludes loss-settlement weeks cannot stand in for matched-window realized ETH wealth.
